title: Adaptive wavelet transform defogging scheme for real-time video restoration with field programmable gate array implementation
tldr: This work proposes an innovative adaptive wavelet transform defogging scheme aimed at precisely modifying the transmittance of the sky and deep fault regions and presents a dedicated field programmable gate array defogging architecture capable of direct application for real-time synchronous defogging of Full HD videos.
abstract: Abstract. In the context of real-time video defogging, accurately estimating the transmittance of sky regions and deep fault regions remains a challenging task due to severe color distortion and halo effects. To address this issue, we propose an innovative adaptive wavelet transform defogging (AWTD) scheme aimed at precisely modifying the transmittance of the sky and deep fault regions. Additionally, we present a dedicated field programmable gate array defogging architecture capable of direct application for real-time synchronous defogging of Full HD (1920×1080) videos. Through extensive experiments and comparisons, we demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed AWTD approach in mitigating color distortion, halo effects, and other fog-induced artifacts. The results show that the dehazing algorithm attains 60 frames per second for the image resolution of 1920×1080, which is suitable of real time applications.

title: Repetitive Action Counting with Feature Interaction Enhancement and Adaptive Gate Fusion
tldr: This work proposes a feature interaction enhancement module designed to improve the learning of action-relevant features from both RGB and skeleton data, and introduces an adaptive local-global attention gating fusion mechanism to integrate enhanced processed RGB and skeleton features.
abstract: Repetitive Action Counting (RAC) aims to count the number of repetitive actions occurring in videos. Accurately identifying these repetitive actions in complex real-world scenes presents several challenges, such as high-frequency periods, action interruption, and background occlusion. Existing methods typically rely on RGB features to calculate feature similarity for motion pattern modeling. However, they inevitably struggle with issues caused by occluded individuals or subtle visual changes. To address these challenges, we first propose a feature interaction enhancement module designed to improve the learning of action-relevant features from both RGB and skeleton data. This mechanism combines the strengths of both RGB and skeleton data, leveraging the complementary nature to enhance the modeling of motion patterns. title: ACE-ProtoNet: Adaptive covariance eigen-gate and uncertainty-aware prototype learning for coronary artery segmentation
tldr: ACE-ProtoNet, a unified framework that couples an Adaptive Covariance Eigen-Gate (ACE-Gate) with an Uncertainty-aware Prototype Learning Head (UPL-Head) to achieve robust and accurate coronary artery segmentation, consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple metrics.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of coronary arteries from Coronary CT Angiography (CCTA) is essential for quantitative stenosis evaluation, plaque characterization, and surgical planning. However, low vessel-to-background contrast, high anatomical variability, and the complex, tree-like vascular morphology pose significant challenges to automated segmentation. To address these challenges, we propose ACE-ProtoNet, a unified framework that couples an Adaptive Covariance Eigen-Gate (ACE-Gate) with an Uncertainty-aware Prototype Learning Head (UPL-Head) to achieve robust and accurate coronary artery segmentation. title: GATE-3D: Geometry-Aware Test-time Adaptive Reranking for Open-Set 3D Shape Retrieval
tldr: GATE-3D, a lightweight query-adaptive reranking method that incorporates geometry without retraining the retrieval backbone, is proposed and found that simple linear routing is more effective than a small MLP in the low-data regime, suggesting that cross-modal disagreement features matter more than model capacity for adaptive routing.
abstract: Large pretrained vision models have substantially improved appearance-based 3D shape retrieval, but they still confuse shapes that look similar while differing in geometry. Although geometry-aware features can reduce these errors, naive fusion of geometry and appearance may hurt retrieval when the two modalities are already well aligned. We propose GATE-3D, a lightweight query-adaptive reranking method that incorporates geometry without retraining the retrieval backbone. For each query, GATE-3D predicts how much a geometry-aware score should adjust the appearance-based ranking using features that capture disagreement between the two modalities. This selective design lets geometry contribute where it helps and stay silent where it would hurt. title: ACE-Net: 3D VFM-CNN Fusion with Adaptive Covariance Eigen-Gate for Coronary Artery Segmentation
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
abstract: Accurate segmentation of coronary arteries from CT angiography is crucial for quantitative stenosis evaluation and surgical planning. This task requires models to capture both global anatomical context and fine-grained local details. While 3D Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) and CNNs are naturally suited for these complementary roles, effectively fusing their heterogeneous feature streams remains a major challenge. To address this, we propose ACE-Net, a unified framework built upon a parallel dual-encoder architecture that couples a 3D foundation model-driven encoder (finetuned from SAM-Med3D) for global structural encoding with a 3D U-Net-based shape encoder for fine-grained local representation. To bridge the feature heterogeneity between the two streams, ACE-Net incorporates the Adaptive Covariance Eigen-Gate (ACE-Gate), which explicitly models interchannel dependencies via covariance analysis and eigenvalue decomposition, enabling adaptive and statistically grounded feature fusion.

title: Gate‐Align‐SED: Semi‐Supervised Sound Event Detection via Adaptive Feature Gating and Cross‐Task Alignment in Situation Awareness
tldr: Gate‐Align‐SED is presented, a unified semi‐supervised framework designed to bridge the gap between clip‐level and frame‐level acoustic modeling for disaster‐related audio understanding, and offers a scalable and generalizable solution for leveraging both weakly labeled and unlabeled data in critical acoustic event recognition scenarios.
abstract: In complex real‐world environments such as disaster monitoring, effective sound event detection (SED) is often hindered by the presence of noise and limited labeled data. This article presents Gate‐Align‐SED, a unified semi‐supervised framework designed to bridge the gap between clip‐level and frame‐level acoustic modeling for disaster‐related audio understanding. The proposed method integrates adaptive feature fusion, mutual attention mechanisms, and a novel label alignment strategy that introduces a learnable correlation matrix to align heterogeneous label granularities. Furthermore, we incorporate a consistency learning paradigm grounded in the Mean‐Teacher framework, promoting robust representation learning across both temporal scales and annotation levels. title: Adaptive Multi-Scale Forecasting and Gate-Localized Conformal Prediction for Multivariate Nonstationary Time Series
tldr: ABF-T-GLCP, a model-agnostic framework for forecasting and uncertainty quantification in nonstationary multivariate time series, shows consistent gains in point forecasting accuracy and substantially narrower prediction intervals with empirical coverage close to the nominal level.
abstract: We propose ABF-T-GLCP, a model-agnostic framework for forecasting and uncertainty quantification in nonstationary multivariate time series. The central idea is to learn an adaptive predictive state representation for point forecasting and reuse it for conformal calibration. The forecasting module combines horizon-specific temporal experts through a learned gate and refines predictions using sparse predictive transfer across related series. The uncertainty module, Gate-Localized Conformal Prediction (GLCP), uses the learned gate state, together with temporal recency, to select locally relevant calibration residuals, thereby coupling uncertainty calibration to the predictive regimes used by the forecasting model. title: Adaptive Throat‐Sieving Gate in a Metal Azolate Framework Enabling Synergistic Equilibrium‐Kinetic Separation of Propylene and Propane
abstract: Developing porous adsorbents for propylene/propane (C3H6/C3H8) separation faces the challenge of integrating high adsorption capacity with fast adsorption kinetics. Herein, we address this challenge through precise pore control in a slightly flexible metal azolate framework NUM‐27a, enabling synergistic equilibrium‐kinetic separation of C3H6/C3H8. title: Concentration-Adaptive AND-Gate Probe Enables High-Fidelity Imaging of miRNA in Live Cells.
tldr: The ATMiR-LOCK probe represents a promising strategy for developing highly specific diagnostic tools for early tumor detection, and demonstrates high sensitivity, with a picomolar detection limit for miR-21, and an effective response to millimolar levels of cellular ATP in cancer cells, both with excellent specificity and reliability.
abstract: The tumor microenvironment is characterized by abnormal endogenous signals, including elevated ATP levels. Developing probes that specifically respond to such signals is essential for accurate tumor detection. While catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) provides efficient, enzyme-free signal amplification, conventional systems suffer from single target design and background signal leakage. To address this, we designed a nucleic acid hybrid probe, termed ATMiR-LOCK (Adenosine Triphosphate and MiRNA Logic Controlled Circuit Key), which integrates a dual-ATP aptamer with two CHA hairpins. This system enables synchronous response to ATP and microRNA-21 (miR-21), an oncogenic miRNA overexpressed in various malignant tumors. title: How Much Memory Do We Need? Adaptive Memory Gate for Neural Operators
tldr: AMGFNO is proposed, which dynamically modulates memory weight through a learnable gate, and achieves 55-79% nRMSE reduction over at low resolution, with the learned gate value automatically decreasing from 0.7 to near-zero as resolution increases.
abstract: Neural operators have emerged as a powerful data-driven approach for solving time-dependent PDEs. Among recent advances, memory-augmented neural operators explicitly incorporate past states and have achieved remarkable performance under low-resolution observation settings. However, existing approaches apply a fixed memory weight regardless of observation conditions, such as resolution or physical parameters, limiting their adaptability. Our preliminary experiments reveal that optimal memory weight varies with resolution and viscosity, implying that a fixed memory weight cannot simultaneously optimize performance across diverse settings. We propose AMGFNO, which dynamically modulates memory weight through a learnable gate. On the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and Burgers'equations, AMGFNO achieves 55-79% nRMSE reduction over at low resolution, with the learned gate value automatically decreasing from $\bar{g} \approx 0.7$ to near-zero as resolution increases.

title: Voltage Balancing of Series-Connected SiC mosfets With Adaptive-Impedance Self-Powered Gate Drivers
venue: IEEE transactions on industrial electronics (1982. Print)
abstract: Passive clamping snubbers for voltage balancing (VB) series-connected power devices exhibit strong applicability and high robustness; moreover, they are particularly suitable for the emerging fast-switching silicon-carbide (SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (mosfets). However, the compromise still exists as a better VB performance comes at a penalty of a larger loss of snubber. title: Adaptive Feature Fusion Gate and Gated Channel-Spatial Attention in CNN-Transformer Models for Music Genre Classification
tldr: The Convolutional Neural Network-Gated Transformer Network (CT-GateNet) is proposed, a hybrid architecture that integrates a gated channel-spatial attention mechanism with an adaptive feature fusion gating mechanism to achieve discriminative feature learning and efficient feature integration.
abstract: With the rapid growth of music data, automatic music genre classification has become a critical task in music information retrieval. Traditional methods based on handcrafted features are increasingly inadequate when handling large-scale analysis. abstract: Multimodal recommendation aims to enhance user preference modeling by leveraging rich item content such as images and text. title: “Too Crowded for a Robot?”: Modeling Human Acceptance Criteria for Elevator-Riding Robots
venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

abstract: Robots are increasingly expected to share elevators with people, yet little is known about the conditions shaping acceptance. We introduce the Robot Boarding Area (RBA)—a designated entry zone for robots—and examine how its availability and congestion affect user evaluations. In an online survey, acceptance sharply decreased once the RBA was occupied by any person or large object, even under moderate crowding. A VR experiment confirmed this pattern and further showed that participants preferred when robots refrained from boarding in crowded conditions compared to forcing entry. By formalizing the RBA as an acceptance criterion and demonstrating the value of adaptive skip strategies, this work identifies spatial availability and boarding behavior as central to socially acceptable robot deployment in elevators.

abstract: This paper introduces a rotational quantum particle swarm optimizer (RQPSO) that updates particles via quantum rotation–gate dynamics on a compact phase representation. abstract: This article investigates the secure and privacy-preserving consensus problem of multiagent systems (MASs) with directed interaction topologies under multiple cyberattacks, which contain deception attacks and DoS attacks. abstract: The Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) paradigm has emerged as a promising solution to scale up model capacity while maintaining inference efficiency. abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) leverages information fusion from diverse modalities (e.g., text, audio, visual) to enhance sentiment prediction. However, simple fusion techniques often fail to account for variations in modality quality, such as those that are noisy, missing, or semantically conflicting. abstract: Speculative Decoding is a prominent technique for accelerating the autoregressive inference of large language models (LLMs) by employing a fast draft model to propose candidate token sequences and a large target model to verify them in parallel. abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) typically process visual inputs as a prefix to the language decoder.
